summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and archaeology, Chirapravati studied at Silpakorn, Ohio State, and Cornell universities. She served at Silpakorn, Tsukuba, the Asian Art Museum, and Sonoma State, and was Associate Professor and Director of Asian Studies at CSU Sacramento (2002–2016).

Working in Indology and religious studies, Konduparti served as Visiting Faculty at Andhra University (2015), Assistant Professor at Alliance University (2016–2017) and REVA University (2017–2021), and Associate Professor at GITAM University in 2021.
Specializing in Indology and computational studies, Visweswaran studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin, attested in 2026.

Bode specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Bern (Ph.D. 1898), UCL, Collège de France, and Pisa, under scholars including Davids, Bendall, Müller-Hess, and Lévi. She taught at UCL (1909–1917) and SOAS (1917).

Malaviya was an Indian scholar and educationist who studied at Muir Central College, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Allahabad. He taught at Government Inter College, Prayagraj, founded Banaras Hindu University in 1916, and served as its Vice Chancellor (1919–1938).

Biardeau specialized in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the École Normale Supérieure de Sèvres, the University of Kerala, and under K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri, and was Professor of Indian Religions at the EPHE (~1956–1989).

Specializing in archaeology and Buddhist studies, Giteau studied under Jean Filliozat and André Bareau at the EPHE and earned a doctorate from Sorbonne Nouvelle. She held posts at the EFEO, National Museum of Cambodia, and Sorbonne Nouvelle.

Hallade worked in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian-Central Asian studies. She studied at the École des Beaux-Arts and École du Louvre under Joseph Hackin and Moritz Abraham Stern, later serving at the Guimet Museum (1935–1965) and École du Louvre.
Deshpande is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Ludo Rocher. He held a long-term professorship at the University of Michigan, attested between 1976 and 2009.
Gore studied at the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and at the Columbia University School of Social Work. He later held an appointment at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1997–2002).

Khanna specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned her D.Phil. from the University of Oxford and held posts attested in 2012 as Director at Jamia Millia Islamia and at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Parameswaran, working in Indology and other fields, received an MD in Dravyagunavijnan from Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (2007–2010). He was an Assistant Professor at Vaidyaratnam P.S. Varier Ayurveda College in 2011, continuing there through at least 2021.
Specializing in Tibetology and archaeology, Balasubramaniam worked as a Project Associate (2018–2020) and completed a PhD (2022) at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras.

Dhaky, an Indologist and historian of architecture, graduated in geology and chemistry from Fergusson College. He founded the Archeology Research Group in Porbandar (1951) and was Associate Director and Director Emeritus of Research at the AIIS (~1976–2005).
Gupta studied at Sanskrit College and Calcutta Medical College. He taught Ayurveda at Sanskrit College (~1830–1835) and later served at Calcutta Medical College (~1835–1856).
An Indologist, Shastri served as Superintendent of the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir, with his tenure attested during 1918–1934 and 1943–1945.
Rimal is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Alberta in 2016 and held a post there attested in 2021.
Vats was a scholar in the fields of archaeology and Indology who succeeded Rakhal Das Banerji (Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay).

Szpindler works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned an M.A. from the University of Warsaw and a doctorate from Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań, serving as Adiunkt at the University of Warsaw in 2019.
Geiger was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Wilhelm Geiger, Hermann Beckh, and Heinrich Lüders.
